hero.headline: Senate prepares for fight over Trump Iran peace deal
hero.body:
The Senate has rejected a Democratic attempt to require President Trump to seek Congressional approval before continuing military operations against Iran. The vote on a war powers resolution introduced by Virginia Democrat Tim Kaine fell along party lines, with Republicans blocking the measure 53-47. Only one Republican, Senator Rand Paul of Kentucky, voted with Democrats, while Pennsylvania Democrat John Fetterman was the sole member of his party to oppose the resolution.

The failed measure would have forced an end to the U.S. air and naval campaign against Iran and required the president to obtain Congressional permission before resuming hostilities. The outcome sets the stage for a broader Senate debate about Trump's authority to wage war without explicit Congressional approval.

Democratic opponents argued the resolution was essential to prevent repeating past foreign policy mistakes. Senator Chris Murphy warned that the conflict risked escalating further, stating: "Here we are in a war that has cost American lives, that is leading to chaos throughout the region, that threatens to go bigger and bigger and bigger."

Tim Kaine emphasized that the Constitution requires Congressional debate on matters of war. He pointed out that the conflict has already resulted in American casualties and urged the Senate to fulfill its constitutional duty.

Republicans defended Trump's military campaign as lawful and necessary. Senator Lindsey Graham argued: "We're here to settle the account with the Iranian regime," noting that Iran had shown unwillingness to compromise during negotiations over its nuclear program. Mitch McConnell contended that Trump's actions fell within established presidential authority as commander-in-chief and compared the campaign to previous military actions by other presidents.

The conflict has claimed six American service members' lives since it began, along with an estimated 1,045 to 1,500 Iranian casualties. Trump initiated the military campaign after months of unsuccessful negotiations with Tehran regarding its nuclear program, though he did notify key lawmakers before proceeding.

The House of Representatives faces a similar war powers resolution on Thursday, introduced by Republican Thomas Massie and Democrat Ro Khanna. That measure also faces long odds of passage, with Speaker Mike Johnson warning it would be "dangerous" to halt ongoing military operations.

Even if both chambers passed a war powers resolution, Trump could veto it. Overriding a presidential veto would require two-thirds majorities in both the House and Senate, a threshold unlikely to be achieved given current Republican support for the president's military decisions.

The failed Senate vote underscores deep divisions over war powers and Trump's approach to foreign policy, with Republicans largely backing the president's authority to conduct military operations without prior Congressional approval.

cards.headline: Israel Orders Strikes on Beirut Suburbs as Hezbollah Conflict Escalates
cards.teaser: Benjamin Netanyahu directed strikes on the Hezbollah stronghold of Dahieh in response to attacks on Israeli civilians.
cards.body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has ordered military strikes on Dahieh, a Hezbollah stronghold in Beirut's southern suburbs, citing attacks on Israeli civilians by the Lebanese militant group. The strikes represent a major escalation, bringing direct military action to Lebanon's capital.

In a related development, Israel has captured the 12th-century Beaufort castle overlooking southern Lebanon and northern Israel, suggesting plans for an extended military presence in the region as the conflict with Hezbollah intensifies.

cards.headline: Former Fed Chair Powell Warns of Credibility Risk from Political Pressure
cards.teaser: Jerome Powell cautioned that the Federal Reserve's credibility would be at risk if presidents could fire central bank officials.
cards.body:
Jerome Powell, the former chair of the Federal Reserve, warned that the central bank's credibility could be damaged by political pressure. Speaking at an award ceremony, Powell said the Fed's public trust would be lost if presidential authority extended to firing Fed officials.

Powell received a Profile in Courage award for his stance. He used the platform to caution against political interference in institutions including the Fed, courts, and schools. His comments come amid what he described as a political stress test on the independence of the central bank.

cards.headline: Trump administration moves to roll back chemical safety rules
cards.teaser: The administration is pursuing deregulation of chemical plant safety standards as recent industrial incidents forced evacuations in California and Washington.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is moving forward with plans to roll back chemical safety regulations despite recent deadly industrial chemical incidents. Last week, about 50,000 people were ordered to evacuate in Southern California after an overheating chemical tank threatened to explode. Those evacuation orders have since been lifted.

Another chemical incident occurred this week in Washington. Critics have expressed outrage at the timing of the deregulatory push, arguing that recent events demonstrate the need for stronger safety standards rather than reduced oversight of chemical facilities.

cards.headline: EEOC moves to overturn decades-old anti-discrimination rules
cards.teaser: The civil rights agency is dismantling tools created to fight employment discrimination.
cards.body:
The Equal Employment Opportunity Commission is working to overturn longstanding rules designed to combat employment discrimination. The Trump administration argues that these existing regulations have resulted in discrimination against white people.

The EEOC is systematically dismantling multiple enforcement tools that have been part of the agency's civil rights mandate for years. This represents a significant shift in how the federal government approaches workplace discrimination prevention based on race, gender, and other protected characteristics.

cards.headline: Senate immigration bill stalls as deadline passes
cards.teaser: The Senate missed its deadline for passing an immigration enforcement funding package after negotiations collapsed over a White House anti-weaponization fund proposal.
cards.body:
The Senate returned to session after missing a deadline to pass an immigration enforcement funding package. Negotiations on the reconciliation bill collapsed more than a week ago following the White House's announcement of a separate anti-weaponization fund that would issue payouts to certain individuals.

The breakdown illustrates ongoing Republican infighting over the immigration measure. The Senate will continue working on the bill this week, but the timeline for reaching President Trump's desk remains uncertain as disputes over the additional fund persist.

cards.headline: Hackers shift from ballot tampering to voter misinformation
cards.teaser: A cybersecurity report finds that foreign actors are focusing on spreading confusion through misinformation rather than targeting voting systems in the 2026 midterms.
cards.body:
Hackers and foreign influence operators are increasingly using misinformation campaigns to confuse and mislead voters rather than tampering with voting machines and ballots in the 2026 midterm elections. A report published by cybersecurity firm Check Point Software identified the shift in tactics.

The report said attempts at phishing, impersonation, and misinformation activity will be the most common threats. The findings suggest that adversaries have changed their approach from direct attacks on election infrastructure to efforts aimed at sowing confusion and distrust among voters through false information campaigns.

hero.headline: Israel Orders Strikes on Beirut Suburbs as Hezbollah Conflict Escalates
hero.teaser: Benjamin Netanyahu directed strikes on the Hezbollah stronghold of Dahieh in response to attacks on Israeli civilians.
hero.body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has ordered military strikes on Dahieh, a Hezbollah stronghold in Beirut's southern suburbs, citing attacks on Israeli civilians by the Lebanese militant group. The strikes represent a major escalation, bringing direct military action to Lebanon's capital.

In a related development, Israel has captured the 12th-century Beaufort castle overlooking southern Lebanon and northern Israel, suggesting plans for an extended military presence in the region as the conflict with Hezbollah intensifies.

cards.headline: Dozens Killed in Explosion at Myanmar Rebel-Held Village
cards.teaser: An explosion flattened a village in rebel-controlled territory, with local authorities attributing the blast to an accident at a mining explosives warehouse.
cards.body:
Dozens of people died when an explosion destroyed a village in Myanmar territory held by rebel forces. Local authorities said the blast originated at a warehouse storing explosives used for mining operations.

The incident occurred in an area controlled by opposition groups fighting Myanmar's military government. The scale of the explosion was sufficient to flatten structures throughout the village, though specific casualty figures and the total number of wounded remain unclear.

cards.headline: France Seizes Sanctioned Russian Oil Tanker With UK Assistance
cards.teaser: The French Navy conducted an operation with British support to seize a Russian oil tanker operating in violation of sanctions.
cards.body:
French President Emmanuel Macron announced that the French Navy boarded an oil tanker subject to international sanctions in the Atlantic Ocean on Sunday. The vessel was sailing from Russia in violation of imposed restrictions.

The operation involved support from multiple partners, including the United Kingdom, and was conducted in compliance with maritime law. Macron stated that it is "unacceptable for ships to circumvent international sanctions," emphasizing the importance of enforcing restrictions on Russian oil exports since the invasion of Ukraine.

cards.headline: Colombia Presidential Election Heads to Runoff
cards.teaser: Abelardo de la Espriella will face a left-wing senator in a June runoff after no candidate secured a majority in the first round.
cards.body:
Colombia's presidential election will proceed to a runoff on June 21 after no candidate secured more than 50 percent of votes in the first round. Far-right lawyer Abelardo de la Espriella won the initial ballot with 43.7 percent of the vote, while left-wing senator Iván Cepeda received 40.9 percent.

Cepeda, a philosopher and human rights activist who has served in the Senate since 2014, was backed by outgoing President Gustavo Petro's party. De la Espriella, a Trump admirer, has risen rapidly in the polls as an outsider candidate. The two will compete for the presidency in the June runoff.

cards.headline: Former Zelensky Aide Accused of Embezzlement Now Crowdfunding Bail
cards.teaser: Andriy Yermak, once a top adviser to Ukraine's president, faces charges of embezzling millions and consulting a fortuneteller on political matters.
cards.body:
Andriy Yermak, who served as a close aide to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, is now crowdfunding money for bail after being charged with embezzling millions of dollars. Prosecutors also accuse him of consulting a fortuneteller when making political decisions.

Yermak held significant influence during his time as Zelensky's right-hand man, involved in key decisions during Ukraine's ongoing conflict with Russia. His fall from power and the nature of the charges represent a dramatic reversal for a figure who once wielded considerable authority in Ukrainian politics.

cards.headline: Syrian Officers Face War Crime Charges in Austria
cards.teaser: Two Assad regime officials who lived in Austria will stand trial on war crime charges, giving Syrian witnesses a chance to confront their alleged torturers.
cards.body:
Austria will hold its first trial of officials from the Assad regime, charging two Syrian officers who had been living in the country with war crimes. The proceedings will allow Syrian witnesses to directly confront the two men, whom they accuse of torture.

The officers managed to hide in plain sight in Austria before being identified and charged. The trial represents a rare opportunity for victims of the Assad government's actions to seek accountability through European courts, as Syria itself has not prosecuted such cases.

cards.headline: More Files

hero.headline: Ebola cases in Congo reach 282 as outbreak continues in eastern province
hero.teaser: Congo reports over 1,000 suspected cases of the Bundibugyo virus strain in Ituri province.
hero.body:
Confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo have reached 282, with the outbreak concentrated in the eastern Ituri province. The Bundibugyo strain of Ebola currently has no approved treatment or vaccine, though health officials report that people infected with the disease can recover with proper care. Five patients have recovered and been discharged from hospitals.

The World Health Organization estimates the death rate for confirmed cases at between 30% and 50%. Health authorities are urging people who develop symptoms to seek immediate medical attention.

cards.headline: Israel orders strikes on Hezbollah stronghold in Beirut suburbs
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says attacks target Dahieh in response to strikes on Israeli civilians.
cards.body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has ordered strikes targeting Dahieh, a Hezbollah stronghold in Beirut's suburbs. Netanyahu said the strikes are in response to attacks on Israeli civilians by the militant group.

The order marks an escalation in the conflict between Israel and Hezbollah as cross-border hostilities intensify between the two sides.

cards.headline: EEOC moves to overturn decades-old anti-discrimination rules
cards.teaser: The civil rights agency is dismantling tools created to fight employment discrimination.
cards.body:
The Equal Employment Opportunity Commission is working to overturn longstanding rules designed to combat employment discrimination. The Trump administration argues that these existing regulations have resulted in discrimination against white people.

The EEOC is systematically dismantling multiple enforcement tools that have been part of the agency's civil rights mandate for years. This represents a significant shift in how the federal government approaches workplace discrimination prevention based on race, gender, and other protected characteristics.

cards.headline: France seizes sanctioned Russian oil tanker with UK assistance
cards.teaser: The French Navy conducted the operation with support from British forces.
cards.body:
The French Navy boarded an oil tanker subject to international sanctions that was sailing from Russia, according to President Emmanuel Macron. The operation took place in the Atlantic Ocean on the high seas with support from the United Kingdom and other partners, conducted in compliance with maritime law.

Macron stated that the seizure was necessary because it is "unacceptable for ships to circumvent international sanctions." The coordinated action demonstrates France and the UK's commitment to enforcing restrictions on Russian maritime commerce.

cards.headline: New York Mayor Mamdani skips annual Israel Day Parade
cards.teaser: Mayor Zohran Mamdani did not attend the celebration along Fifth Avenue.
cards.body:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani did not attend the annual Israel Day Parade, which took place along Fifth Avenue. The absence marks a departure from the typical mayoral participation in major community events.

The parade proceeded with thousands of spectators gathering to participate in the annual celebration.

cards.headline: UK wins court ruling on collapsed Rwanda asylum agreement
cards.teaser: A court decided the UK does not need to pay Rwanda after pulling out of the deal.
cards.body:
A UK court has ruled that the country does not need to pay Rwanda following the termination of their asylum deal. The agreement, which would have seen asylum seekers processed in Rwanda, collapsed before it could be implemented.

The court's decision resolves the dispute over Britain's financial obligations to Rwanda after withdrawing from the arrangement.

cards.headline: Former Scottish leader calls for joint inquiry into Murrell case
cards.teaser: Jack McConnell supports a dual probe by Holyrood and Westminster into the former SNP chief executive.
cards.body: Former first minister Jack McConnell has backed a proposal for both the Scottish Parliament and Westminster to hold a joint inquiry into crimes involving Peter Murrell. Murrell previously served as chief executive of the Scottish National Party. McConn

hero.body:
Jerome Powell, the former chair of the Federal Reserve, warned that the central bank's credibility could be damaged by political pressure. Speaking at an award ceremony, Powell said the Fed's public trust would be lost if presidential authority extended to firing Fed officials.

Powell received a Profile in Courage award for his stance. He used the platform to caution against political interference in institutions including the Fed, courts, and schools. His comments come amid what he described as a political stress test on the independence of the central bank.

cards.headline: Berkshire Hathaway to Acquire Homebuilder Taylor Morrison for $6.8 Billion
cards.teaser: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway agreed to buy Taylor Morrison in the first major acquisition under CEO Greg Abel.
cards.body:
Berkshire Hathaway announced it would purchase homebuilder Taylor Morrison for $6.8 billion. The deal represents the first significant takeover since Greg Abel became chief executive of the investment conglomerate. Some reports valued the transaction at $8.5 billion including debt.

The acquisition marks a major bet on the U.S. housing market by Berkshire. Taylor Morrison is a publicly traded homebuilder, and the purchase gives Berkshire expanded exposure to residential construction. The deal signals Abel's willingness to pursue large transactions as he leads the company following Warren Buffett's transition from the CEO role.

cards.headline: China's Military Sought Nvidia Chips for Years Despite U.S. Restrictions
cards.teaser: An analysis of procurement records shows the People's Liberation Army openly attempted to acquire restricted American technology.
cards.body:
An analysis of procurement records spanning six years shows that the People's Liberation Army openly pursued restricted Nvidia chips through official purchasing channels. The U.S. maintains export controls on these semiconductors due to their potential use in military and artificial intelligence applications.

The findings reveal sustained efforts by Chinese military entities to acquire advanced semiconductor technology despite American restrictions designed to limit access to such capabilities.

cards.headline: Nvidia Releases New AI Chip for Personal Computers
cards.teaser: The chip maker introduced new technology for consumer PCs as CEO Jensen Huang described it as a reinvention of the computer.
cards.body:
Nvidia announced a new artificial intelligence chip designed for personal computers, with Chief Executive Jensen Huang describing the release as a reinvention of the computer. The chip brings AI processing capabilities directly to Windows PCs, shifting advanced computing from data centers to individual machines.

The announcement reflects Nvidia's expanding role in the AI boom. The company has emerged as a central player in the sector as demand for its processors continues to surge, driving enthusiasm around AI technology in financial markets.

cards.headline: Japanese and South Korean Stock Markets Reach Record Levels
cards.teaser: Equity markets in Japan and South Korea hit new highs despite rising oil prices linked to tensions over Iran.
cards.body:
Stock markets in Japan and South Korea reached record levels. The gains came even as oil prices increased due to concerns about the fragility of an end to conflict involving Iran.

The Asian markets advanced despite global uncertainty around energy supplies. Investors in the region appeared to focus on domestic economic factors and technology sector strength. The record highs contrast with the volatility in commodity markets driven by geopolitical developments in the Middle East.

cards.headline: Nvidia Announces Humanoid Robot Platform for Academic Research
cards.teaser: The chip maker introduced a reference robot based on its Isaac GR00T system, partnering with robotics company Unitree.
cards.body:
Nvidia has unveiled the Isaac GR00T, a humanoid robot platform designed for academic research. The initiative builds on a partnership with Unitree, a Chinese robotics startup that is exploring a public offering.

Nvidia plans to expand these robotics efforts by collaborating with manufacturers in the United States and Europe alongside its work with Unitree. The company has released open-source tools for developing physical AI systems, marking its broader expansion into robotics beyond its traditional graphics processing business.

cards.headline: Investment Firm Considers Takeover Bid for EasyJet
cards.teaser: U.S. investment firm Castlelake is weighing an offer for the budget airline, which called the potential approach opportunistic.
cards.body: American investment firm Castlelake is considering making a takeover offer for EasyJet. The budget airline responded by characterizing any potential bid as opportunistic

hero.headline: CERN detects particle behavior that defies current physics theory
hero.body:
Physicists at CERN's Large Hadron Collider observed a particle behaving in a way that contradicts theoretical predictions, marking the strongest indication yet of physics beyond the Standard Model. The observation reached high statistical significance, suggesting the anomaly is unlikely to be a measurement error or random fluctuation.

The Standard Model has been the foundation of particle physics for decades, describing how fundamental particles interact through three of the four known forces. While the model has successfully predicted numerous experimental results, physicists have long suspected it is incomplete. The theory cannot account for dark matter, dark energy, or gravity at quantum scales.

The detection occurred at the world's largest and most powerful particle accelerator, located near Geneva, Switzerland. The Large Hadron Collider accelerates protons to nearly the speed of light before smashing them together, allowing scientists to study the resulting particles and forces. CERN operates the facility as an international collaboration involving thousands of scientists from over 100 countries.

The observed behavior suggests the existence of forces or particles not included in the Standard Model. Scientific American described these findings as involving exotic particles that could fundamentally change our understanding of physics. The high significance level of the result means the probability of the observation being a statistical fluke is very low, though physicists typically require multiple independent confirmations before declaring a discovery.

If confirmed through additional experiments, the finding could open new areas of research and potentially explain phenomena that current theory cannot address. The discovery process in particle physics often takes years, as researchers must rule out alternative explanations and verify their results through repeated measurements. CERN scientists will continue analyzing data from the collider to determine whether the anomaly represents a genuine deviation from known physics or requires adjustments to experimental methods or theoretical calculations.

cards.headline: Meteor explodes over Massachusetts, producing loud boom
cards.teaser: A meteor entered the atmosphere and exploded off the coast of Massachusetts, creating a loud boom heard by residents.
cards.body:
A meteor exploded over northeastern Massachusetts and southeastern New Hampshire on Saturday afternoon, creating a blast equivalent to 300 tons of TNT. The fireball broke apart at an altitude of 40 miles while traveling at 75,000 miles per hour, according to NASA.

The explosion produced loud booms that resonated across the region. When meteors enter Earth's atmosphere at such extreme speeds, the intense heat and pressure causes them to break apart, generating sonic booms audible over wide areas.

cards.headline: Arm, IBM and Hewlett Packard shares rise as Nvidia chip news extends software rally
cards.teaser: Shares of Arm, IBM and Hewlett Packard rose following Nvidia chip developments that extended a rally in software stocks.
cards.body:
Nvidia announced the RTX Spark, marking its entry into the consumer PC chip market alongside Intel, AMD, Apple, and Qualcomm. The chip represents a complete computing solution designed for laptops and mini-PCs, not just graphics processing.

The announcement triggered gains across the technology sector, with Arm, IBM, and Hewlett Packard shares climbing in trading. Nvidia's chip developments have historically driven significant movement in related technology stocks as investors evaluate implications for the broader computing industry.

cards.headline: Nvidia announces DLSS 4.5 with improved ray reconstruction for August release
cards.teaser: Nvidia will release DLSS 4.5 in August, bringing improved ray reconstruction technology to RTX 20, 30, 40 and 50 series graphics cards.
cards.body:
Nvidia unveiled the second generation of its transformer-based ray reconstruction technology at Computex, set to launch in August. DLSS 4.5 will enhance raytracing performance across multiple generations of RTX graphics cards, from the RTX 20 series through the newer RTX 50 series.

The ray reconstruction feature uses artificial intelligence to improve the quality of raytraced lighting and reflections in games. By extending support to older hardware dating back to 2018, Nvidia allows gamers with earlier graphics cards to benefit from the technology. Over 1,000 games and applications now support RTX technology.

cards.headline: Dell launches $699 XPS 13 laptop with touchscreen to compete with Apple
cards.teaser: Dell introduced a $699 touchscreen XPS 13 laptop, positioning the device as a competitor to Apple's MacBook Neo.
cards.body:
Dell has announced a new XPS 13 laptop designed to rival Apple's MacBook Neo. The device will launch in July at a promotional student price of $699, with a standard starting price of $699 for general consumers. The introductory pricing is available through September for back-to-school shopping.

This marks Dell's return to the XPS 13 line as a more affordable option in the premium laptop segment. The move represents the company's strategy to challenge Apple at a competitive price point while maintaining the XPS brand's position in the high-end Windows laptop market.

cards.headline: AMD releases Radeon RX 9070 GRE graphics card globally for $550
cards.teaser: AMD launched the Radeon RX 9070 GRE graphics card worldwide, pricing the model at $550 with availability starting June 2.
cards.body:
The graphics card features 48 RDNA 4 cores and 12 GB of memory. AMD claims the RX 9070 GRE performs up to 22 percent faster than competing cards in its price range. The model was previously available only in China before the global expansion.

The RX 9070 GRE fills the gap in AMD's product lineup between the RX 9060 XT and RX 9070 models. The pricing positions the card in the mid-range graphics market, competing directly with Nvidia's offerings at similar price points.

cards.headline: AMD announces new Ryzen processors including revived 5800X3D model
cards.teaser: AMD introduced the Ryzen 7 7700X3D and brought back the Ryzen 7 5800X3D as a 10th anniversary edition to address high memory costs.
cards.body:
AMD is relaunching older processor components at Computex 2026, offering an alternative to expensive platform upgrades. The strategy lets PC gamers boost performance without purchasing new motherboards or DDR5 memory.

The Ryzen 7 5800X3D 10th Anniversary Edition marks a decade of AMD's AM4 platform, priced at $349. This approach allows customers to upgrade within existing systems, reducing the overall cost of performance improvements during a period of high memory prices.

hero.headline: Rugby league coach and broadcaster John Kear dies at 71
hero.teaser: John Kear, who coached both England and Wales rugby league teams and worked as a broadcaster, has died.
hero.body:
John Kear, the former England and Wales rugby league coach and respected broadcaster, has died at age 71. The Rugby Football League announced that Kear passed away on Sunday while returning from covering Wigan's Challenge Cup victory at Wembley for the BBC.

Kear had an extensive coaching career spanning more than 700 matches across nine different clubs. He achieved significant success during his time in the sport, most notably guiding Sheffield Eagles to a shock Challenge Cup victory in 1998. He later led Hull FC to Challenge Cup glory in 2005, cementing his reputation as one of rugby league's most accomplished coaches.

Beyond his achievements in club rugby league, Kear represented his country at the highest level. He served as head coach of both the England and Wales national teams, bringing his expertise and tactical knowledge to international competition. His work at international level demonstrated his standing within the sport.

In the later stages of his career, Kear transitioned into broadcasting and became a well-known figure in rugby league media. He provided commentary and analysis for major matches, including the Challenge Cup final coverage for the BBC that he was returning from when he died. His broadcasting work meant he remained a prominent presence in the sport even after stepping back from coaching duties.

Kear's death came the day after he had covered one of rugby league's showcase events, the Challenge Cup final, for the BBC. His passing marked the loss of a significant figure in rugby league circles, where he had built a legacy across both coaching and media over many decades.

His career trajectory from club coaching to international level demonstrated his growing influence in the sport. The Challenge Cup wins with Sheffield Eagles and Hull FC represent particular career highlights, as these victories came against the odds and showcased his ability to prepare teams for major occasions.

The rugby league community recognised Kear as a dedicated figure in the sport throughout his long career. Whether through his work on the sidelines with various clubs or his analysis and commentary in broadcasting roles, he contributed substantially to rugby league across multiple decades. His knowledge of the game and experience at both domestic and international levels made him a respected voice in the sport.

The announcement of his death came from the Rugby Football League, the sport's governing body, reflecting the official recognition of his significance to the game. Kear's contributions to rugby league, from his coaching achievements to his broadcasting work, meant his loss was felt across the sport's community.

cards.headline: Illinois House blocks Chicago Bears stadium funding bill after Senate approval
cards.teaser: The Illinois House of Representatives rejected a stadium funding bill for the Chicago Bears after it passed the state Senate late Sunday, ending efforts to secu.
cards.body:
The Illinois House of Representatives allowed a stadium funding bill for the Chicago Bears to die without a vote as the legislative session ended, despite the measure passing the state Senate late Sunday. The bill failed to advance before the midnight deadline.

The proposed legislation would have provided state support for a new Bears stadium. Without the state funding package, the team will need to pursue alternative financing strategies or reconsider its stadium plans. Lawmakers are exploring whether to revive stadium legislation in future sessions.

cards.headline: James Milner retires after 24 seasons in Premier League
cards.teaser: Former England international James Milner announced his retirement after a career spanning nearly a quarter century in English soccer's top division.
cards.body:
James Milner has announced his retirement at age 40 after a remarkable 24-season Premier League career. The former England international, who made 61 caps for his country, holds the record for most Premier League appearances with 658, a milestone he reached while playing for Brighton against Brentford in February.

Milner began his career at Leeds, his boyhood club, and spent his final three seasons at Brighton. Reflecting on his journey, the veteran midfielder said he "could never have dreamed" of such a career, cementing his legacy as one of English soccer's most durable and accomplished players.

cards.headline: Liverpool dismisses Arne Slot as head coach
cards.teaser: Liverpool sacked head coach Arne Slot, who said he is leaving the club among Europe's elite teams.
cards.body:
Arne Slot has been sacked by Liverpool, just over a year after winning the Premier League title in his debut season. The 47-year-old's departure follows a dramatic decline in his second year with the club.

In an open letter, Slot thanked Liverpool supporters for a connection that "goes beyond football" and said the club has the foundations to compete at the highest level for years to come. Meanwhile, Liverpool is moving quickly to find his successor, with formal talks planned with Andoni Iraola this week. The club also plans to speak with Stuttgart's Sebastian Hoeness and Pierre Sage of Lens, hoping to appoint a new head coach before the World Cup.

cards.headline: Crystal Palace to interview Lens manager Pierre Sage for head coach position
cards.teaser: Crystal Palace is scheduled to meet with Lens manager Pierre Sage as the club searches for a replacement for Oliver Glasner.
cards.body:
Crystal Palace are set to hold talks with Pierre Sage, the manager of French club Lens, as they search for a new head coach. The discussions come following Oliver Glasner's departure from the Premier League club.

Sage is currently managing Lens in France's top division and is among the candidates being considered for the vacant position at Selhurst Park.

cards.headline: Pirates place pitcher Carmen Mlodzinski on restricted list
cards.teaser: The Pittsburgh Pirates moved right-hander Carmen Mlodzinski to the restricted list after he was not ready to pitch.
cards.body:
The Pittsburgh Pirates placed pitcher Carmen Mlodzinski on the restricted list after he was not prepared to pitch in a scheduled appearance. The team made the roster move involving the right-handed pitcher.

Mlodzinski was slated to pitch but the Pirates determined he was not ready for the assignment. The restricted list placement raises questions about Mlodzinski's status with the organization going forward.

cards.headline: 15-year-old IPL player Vaibhav Sooryavanshi wins car but cannot drive it yet
cards.teaser: Indian Premier League teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi received a car as an award but will have to wait three years before he can legally drive it.
cards.body:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, a 15-year-old cricket sensation, won a car as recognition for his outstanding performances in the Indian Premier League. The teenage player received the vehicle as an award at the IPL awards ceremony.

However, Sooryavanshi will have to wait three years before he can legally drive the car he won. The young cricketer is currently below India's legal driving age, meaning the award sits unused for now.

hero.headline: Joe Negri, Handyman Negri on Mister Rogers' Neighborhood, Dies at 99
hero.body:
Joe Negri, the jazz guitarist who portrayed Handyman Negri on the children's television series Mister Rogers' Neighborhood, has died at 99, just days before his 100th birthday. The Pittsburgh-based musician and actor was a fixture on the program for decades, bringing his warmth and musical talent to generations of young viewers.

Negri appeared regularly on Mister Rogers' Neighborhood as the affable handyman character, often helping neighbors with repairs while sharing his love of music. His role made him a beloved figure to millions of children who grew up watching the show, which aired from 1968 to 2001. Beyond his television work, Negri was a highly respected jazz guitarist with a career spanning more than seven decades.

A virtuoso in the jazz world, Negri performed with numerous prominent musicians throughout his career and was considered a master of his instrument. He recorded multiple albums and was a sought-after session musician. His ability to connect with audiences of all ages made him uniquely suited to his dual career in both jazz performance and children's television. Negri's gentle demeanor and genuine kindness mirrored the values Fred Rogers championed on the show.

The musician's passing comes as Pittsburgh and the broader entertainment community prepare to mark what would have been his centennial birthday. Negri remained active in music and maintained connections to the Mister Rogers' Neighborhood legacy throughout his life. His contributions to both jazz music and children's programming left a lasting impact on American culture.

Negri's death represents the loss of one of the last remaining regular cast members from the original run of Mister Rogers' Neighborhood. His work on the show helped create a nurturing environment that shaped childhood experiences for multiple generations of Americans. The combination of his musical excellence and his gentle presence on screen made him an irreplaceable part of public television history.

cards.headline: Matt Brown, Star of Alaskan Bush People, Found Dead in Washington River at 42
cards.teaser: The reality television personality's body was recovered from a river, with his brother Noah helping to pull him from the water.
cards.body:
Matt Brown, known for his role on the Discovery Channel reality series Alaskan Bush People, was found dead in a river in Washington state at 42. His brother Noah Brown assisted in recovering his body from the water.

Brown appeared on Alaskan Bush People, which followed his family's life living off the grid in remote Alaska. The show documented the Brown family's survival skills and unconventional lifestyle, attracting a dedicated audience over multiple seasons. Matt was one of the eldest children in the Brown family featured on the program.

cards.headline: Sam Levinson Says Euphoria Ends With Season 3
cards.teaser: The creator described the HBO series finale as a tragic but honest conclusion to the story.
cards.body:
Euphoria will end with its third season, creator Sam Levinson confirmed. The HBO drama, which debuted in 2019 and starred Zendaya as Rue, became a cultural phenomenon following teenagers grappling with addiction and trauma.

Levinson defended the season finale's major character death, saying it felt like an honest conclusion to the story he wanted to tell. He described the narrative as tragic but truthful to the vision he set out to create.

cards.headline: Jimmy Kimmel Receives Peabody Award, Tony Gilroy Urges Action Against Fascism
cards.teaser: Jimmy Kimmel Live was among 34 winners at the Peabody Awards ceremony, while Andor creator delivered a pointed speech.
cards.body:
Jimmy Kimmel Live was among 34 winners selected by the Peabody Awards jury this year. Kimmel joked during his acceptance speech that he felt unintelligent being honored alongside documentaries and serious news programming. He thanked "Pumpkin McPornhumper" Trump in jest during his remarks.

Andor creator Tony Gilroy also accepted a Peabody Award and used his speech to call on the audience to confront fascism before it takes hold. He referenced the Empire from his Star Wars work while delivering his message.

cards.headline: Zee Entertainment Secures FIFA Soccer Rights in India Through 2034
cards.teaser: The deal covers 39 FIFA events including multiple World Cups on Indian broadcast and streaming platforms.
cards.body:
Zee Entertainment Enterprises secured Indian broadcast and streaming rights to 39 FIFA soccer events spanning 2026 to 2034. The package includes the FIFA World Cup 2026, FIFA World Cup 2030, and FIFA Women's World Cup 2027, the company announced.

This marks the first partnership between Zee and FIFA. The agreement also covers a portfolio of age-group tournaments and futsal competitions. The multi-year deal positions Zee as the exclusive Indian broadcaster for major international soccer events over the next eight years.

cards.headline: Hasan Piker and Cenk Uygur Barred From Entering UK for SXSW London
cards.teaser: The Home Office denied entry to the Twitch streamer and broadcaster, preventing their scheduled conference appearances.
cards.body:
UK Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood barred Twitch streamer Hasan Piker and broadcaster Cenk Uygur from entering the United Kingdom. The decision prevents them from attending SXSW London, where they were scheduled to appear.

Piker is a popular political commentator on Twitch, while Uygur is his uncle and a prominent broadcaster. Both were set to participate in panels at the South by Southwest festival's London edition. The UK Home Office and SXSW London issued statements following the decision.

cards.headline: Mick Jagger Says Rolling Stones Will Tour Again After 2026
cards.teaser: The musician confirmed no tour will happen in 2026 but said the band will return to the road as soon as possible.
cards.body:
Mick Jagger said he cannot wait to tour with the Rolling Stones again. The musician confirmed a tour will not take place in 2026 but expressed eagerness to get back on the road.

Jagger indicated the band plans to tour as soon as possible

hero.headline: Senate prepares for fight over Trump Iran peace deal
hero.body:
The Senate has rejected a Democratic attempt to require President Trump to seek Congressional approval before continuing military operations against Iran. The vote on a war powers resolution introduced by Virginia Democrat Tim Kaine fell along party lines, with Republicans blocking the measure 53-47. Only one Republican, Senator Rand Paul of Kentucky, voted with Democrats, while Pennsylvania Democrat John Fetterman was the sole member of his party to oppose the resolution.

The failed measure would have forced an end to the U.S. air and naval campaign against Iran and required the president to obtain Congressional permission before resuming hostilities. The outcome sets the stage for a broader Senate debate about Trump's authority to wage war without explicit Congressional approval.

Democratic opponents argued the resolution was essential to prevent repeating past foreign policy mistakes. Senator Chris Murphy warned that the conflict risked escalating further, stating: "Here we are in a war that has cost American lives, that is leading to chaos throughout the region, that threatens to go bigger and bigger and bigger."

Tim Kaine emphasized that the Constitution requires Congressional debate on matters of war. He pointed out that the conflict has already resulted in American casualties and urged the Senate to fulfill its constitutional duty.

Republicans defended Trump's military campaign as lawful and necessary. Senator Lindsey Graham argued: "We're here to settle the account with the Iranian regime," noting that Iran had shown unwillingness to compromise during negotiations over its nuclear program. Mitch McConnell contended that Trump's actions fell within established presidential authority as commander-in-chief and compared the campaign to previous military actions by other presidents.

The conflict has claimed six American service members' lives since it began, along with an estimated 1,045 to 1,500 Iranian casualties. Trump initiated the military campaign after months of unsuccessful negotiations with Tehran regarding its nuclear program, though he did notify key lawmakers before proceeding.

The House of Representatives faces a similar war powers resolution on Thursday, introduced by Republican Thomas Massie and Democrat Ro Khanna. That measure also faces long odds of passage, with Speaker Mike Johnson warning it would be "dangerous" to halt ongoing military operations.

Even if both chambers passed a war powers resolution, Trump could veto it. Overriding a presidential veto would require two-thirds majorities in both the House and Senate, a threshold unlikely to be achieved given current Republican support for the president's military decisions.

The failed Senate vote underscores deep divisions over war powers and Trump's approach to foreign policy, with Republicans largely backing the president's authority to conduct military operations without prior Congressional approval.

cards.headline: Senate immigration bill stalls as deadline passes
cards.teaser: The Senate missed its deadline for passing an immigration enforcement funding package after negotiations collapsed over a White House anti-weaponization fund proposal.
cards.body:
The Senate returned to session after missing a deadline to pass an immigration enforcement funding package. Negotiations on the reconciliation bill collapsed more than a week ago following the White House's announcement of a separate anti-weaponization fund that would issue payouts to certain individuals.

The breakdown illustrates ongoing Republican infighting over the immigration measure. The Senate will continue working on the bill this week, but the timeline for reaching President Trump's desk remains uncertain as disputes over the additional fund persist.

cards.headline: Trump administration moves to roll back chemical safety rules
cards.teaser: The administration is pursuing deregulation of chemical plant safety standards as recent industrial incidents forced evacuations in California and Washington.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is moving forward with plans to roll back chemical safety regulations despite recent deadly industrial chemical incidents. Last week, about 50,000 people were ordered to evacuate in Southern California after an overheating chemical tank threatened to explode. Those evacuation orders have since been lifted.

Another chemical incident occurred this week in Washington. Critics have expressed outrage at the timing of the deregulatory push, arguing that recent events demonstrate the need for stronger safety standards rather than reduced oversight of chemical facilities.

cards.headline: Becerra surges to front in California governor's race
cards.teaser: Former Health and Human Services Secretary Xavier Becerra has moved from single-digit polling to become a top contender ahead of the California primary.
cards.body:
Former Health and Human Services Secretary Xavier Becerra appears positioned to finish as one of the front-runners in the race to succeed California Gov. Gavin Newsom. Becerra polled in single digits just a few months ago but has gained significant momentum heading into the primary.

Democrats attribute Becerra's rise to several factors, including former Rep. Eric Swalwell's exit from the race. The shift represents a significant turnaround for a candidate who had struggled to gain traction earlier in the campaign. California's unusual primary system and a low-profile field have made this year's gubernatorial race difficult to predict.

cards.headline: Trump backs federal control over prediction market regulation
cards.teaser: The president is supporting efforts to block state restrictions on prediction markets as federal and state regulators compete for authority over the platforms.
cards.body:
President Trump is supporting an effort to prevent states from restricting prediction markets, wading into a regulatory dispute that has divided Republicans. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission has brought cases against more than half a dozen states over their attempts to regulate the platforms.

The issue pits federal regulators against state authorities in a legal fight over who has jurisdiction over prediction markets. The dispute has created splits within the GOP between those who favor federal oversight and those who support state regulatory authority over the emerging industry.

cards.headline: Hackers shift from ballot tampering to voter misinformation
cards.teaser: A cybersecurity report finds that foreign actors are focusing on spreading confusion through misinformation rather than targeting voting systems in the 2026 midterms.
cards.body:
Hackers and foreign influence operators are increasingly using misinformation campaigns to confuse and mislead voters rather than tampering with voting machines and ballots in the 2026 midterm elections. A report published by cybersecurity firm Check Point Software identified the shift in tactics.

The report said attempts at phishing, impersonation, and misinformation activity will be the most common threats. The findings suggest that adversaries have changed their approach from direct attacks on election infrastructure to efforts aimed at sowing confusion and distrust among voters through false information campaigns.

cards.headline: Maine Democrat tests voter tolerance for scandal
cards.teaser: Senate candidate Graham Platner faces setbacks as recent reporting raises questions about whether Democrats will accept scandal-plagued candidates.
cards.body:
Maine Senate candidate Graham Platner is testing whether Democrats are willing to elect candidates despite significant scandals, following a pattern that Republicans embraced with Donald Trump. Platner suffered his latest setback when the Wall Street Journal and New York Times reported new information about his background.

The race will show whether voter tolerance for scandal has become a broader feature of American politics beyond Trump-specific phenomena. Democrats have traditionally held their candidates to stricter ethical standards, but Platner's candidacy could signal a shift in how the party approaches candidates with troubled pasts.
